cultivar: Mainly medium- and small-leaf population tea
processing: Fine buds and young leaves, one bud with one leaf at the Qingming picking, are made into a green tea finished flat or curled. The well-known Bikou tea is described as hand-finished.
harvest_season: Spring around Qingming is the prized one-bud-one-leaf picking. Fewer picking rounds in the year are part of how the tea is described.
appearance_dry: Flat, smooth and even in green with a slight yellow cast, or curled; the bud and leaf show as a spear and flag.
appearance_wet: Even leaf, with bud and leaf standing apart as spear and flag.
taste_profile: A clean, high, orchid-like aroma that lasts, over a brisk, mellow and fresh sweetness.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a flat-style green rather than a local rule: a glass shows the spear-and-flag leaves well, and water just below boiling brings out the aroma without bitterness. Bikou tea is said to steep well more than once.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year spring tea, with the Qingming picking the one to look for, and best within about a year. The Wenxian label unified the county's tea brands from 2014.
description:
Wenxian Green Tea is grown in the far south of Gansu, on the Sichuan border, in one of the country's more northerly tea areas. The protected area is four townships: Bikou, Zhongmiao, Fanba and Liujiaping, where the climate is damp and relatively low for this rugged county. Bikou is the best-known name.

The tea comes mainly from medium- and small-leaf population plants, with fewer picking rounds in a year than in warmer provinces. Spring picks are one bud with one leaf, which open in the cup as the classic spear and flag.

The cup is clear with a high, lasting aroma often compared with orchid, and a brisk, fresh sweetness. It suits a glass and water a little off the boil. It is reported to have relatively high amino acids and caffeine, so it can be stronger than its pale colour suggests.

Buy by harvest and look for Qingming-time tea. Flat and curled shapes both exist, and they are the same appellation, so taste rather than shape should decide.
history:
Tea growing in Wenxian is traced in historical records to the Daoguang reign of the Qing dynasty. Bikou green tea, finely picked and hand-finished, became the county's best-known name.

The tea received national geographical indication protection on 26 September 2013. From 2014 the county merged its tea labels under a single Wenxian Green Tea brand and built a tea museum and farm-stays around it, with about 68,000 mu of gardens reported in Bikou, Zhongmiao and Fanba.
